entity_title: Changing employer under the Labor Reform Initiative
fact_text: Since the 2021 Labor Reform Initiative an expatriate can move to another private-sector employer without the old kafala 'release'. The new employer applies through the Qiwa portal; the worker must generally have completed one calendar year with the current employer (counted from entry to the Kingdom) and served the contractual notice period.
evidence_quote: A service that allows expatriate workers to transfer jobs between private-sector establishments according to specific regulations

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: a work visa ties you to one sponsor for the whole contract and you cannot switch. Actually: the LRI lets you transfer employer via Qiwa after ~1 year plus notice. Action: check your Kingdom-entry date and remaining notice before assuming you are locked in.

entity_title: Transfer without the current employer's consent
fact_text: In specific breach situations an expatriate may transfer to a new employer without the current employer's approval, including: no contract registered within 3 months of entry, three consecutive months unpaid, the employer being absent (travel/imprisonment/death), or an expired work permit or residency visa.
evidence_quote: Conditions under which expatriate workers are entitled to employee transfer without conditions

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: you always need your sponsor to sign off before moving. Actually: the LRI lists conditions where transfer is allowed without consent. Action: if you have gone 3 months unpaid or your permit/visa has expired, you may apply to transfer via Qiwa without a release.

entity_title: Exit/Re-entry visa is under the worker's control
fact_text: An Iqama holder needs an Exit and Re-entry Visa (applied for on the Absher portal) to leave and lawfully return to Saudi Arabia. Under the automatic exit/re-entry service the employer does not bear the cost and, crucially, the employer is not entitled to cancel a worker's valid Exit and Re-entry Visa.
evidence_quote: The employer is not entitled to cancel the worker’s valid

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: your employer controls whether and when you can leave the country. Actually: the worker applies via Absher and the employer cannot cancel a valid exit/re-entry visa. Action: manage your own exit/re-entry visa in Absher before any trip; do not rely on HR to open or close it.

entity_title: Extending an exit/re-entry visa from abroad via Muqeem
fact_text: If you are already outside Saudi Arabia and your Exit and Re-entry Visa is about to expire, it can be extended through the Muqeem platform (fee 200 SAR) while you are abroad. Letting it lapse can block your lawful return.
evidence_quote: This service allows extending the exit and return visa for those outside the Kingdom through Muqeem platform

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: once abroad there is nothing you can do if your re-entry visa is expiring. Actually: it can be extended remotely via Muqeem. Action: if a trip runs long, have your sponsor extend the exit/re-entry visa in Muqeem before it expires rather than risk being unable to re-enter.

entity_title: Iqama issuance requires a medical exam and is done by the sponsor
fact_text: The Resident ID (Iqama) for an expatriate and their family members is issued by the sponsor electronically via Absher, and issuance requires passing a medical examination at approved medical centers (issuance fee 600 SAR). The expatriate must be physically in Saudi Arabia and not registered as absent from work.
evidence_quote: Passing the medical examination for a family member or an expatriate in approved

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: the entry work visa is your residence permit. Actually: you still need an Iqama issued after arrival, and it depends on a medical exam at an approved centre. Action: complete the required medical test at an approved centre so your (and your family's) Iqama can be issued and renewed.

entity_title: Employment contract must be documented in Qiwa
fact_text: The employment contract must be created and documented electronically in Qiwa. The employee can approve, reject or request changes to it from their Qiwa Individuals account, and it is only officially documented by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development once both parties agree.
evidence_quote: If both parties agree, the contract is then officially documented by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: a signed paper offer letter is your binding contract. Actually: the enforceable contract is the one documented in Qiwa with your electronic approval. Action: log into Qiwa Individuals and confirm the documented contract matches your offer before you rely on its terms.

entity_title: 183 days makes you a Saudi tax resident
fact_text: Residing in Saudi Arabia for more than 183 days lets an individual obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from ZATCA (issued free), used to claim exemption from home-country tax under double-taxation treaties. Saudi Arabia levies no personal income tax on employment salaries.
evidence_quote: Residence in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for more than 183 days.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: tax residency is decided only by your home country. Actually: crossing 183 days in the Kingdom makes you a Saudi tax resident and you can get a ZATCA certificate to avoid double taxation. Action: request a ZATCA Tax Residency Certificate once past 183 days to support relief in your home country.

entity_title: Premium Residency: work and change jobs with no sponsor
fact_text: A Premium Residency Permit holder (and their family) may be employed in private-sector establishments and change jobs within that sector without an employer sponsor, and may exit and re-enter the Kingdom without a visa. It is a paid alternative to sponsorship-based residence.
evidence_quote: Employment of the permit holder and any of his/her family members in private sector

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: every foreign worker must have a Saudi employer sponsor (kafala). Actually: Premium Residency removes the sponsor tie, allows free job changes and visa-free exit/entry. Action: for senior/long-term relocations, evaluate Premium Residency instead of standard sponsored residence.

entity_title: Cooperative health insurance is a legal precondition of residence
fact_text: Holding a medical insurance policy under the Cooperative Health Insurance Law is a legal precondition tied to residence in Saudi Arabia. A Premium Residency applicant, for example, must provide such a policy within 30 days of approval; for sponsored workers the employer is required to arrange cooperative health insurance covering the worker and dependents.
evidence_quote: provide a medical insurance policy in accordance with the Cooperative Health Insurance Law

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: health insurance is optional or you can buy any plan. Actually: a cooperative health insurance policy meeting the statutory law is required and is linked to residence status. Action: confirm your employer has enrolled you and your family in a compliant cooperative policy, as it is needed for Iqama issuance/renewal.

entity_title: Foreign licence holders can convert without the driving test
fact_text: Residents who hold a valid foreign or international driving licence can skip the driving-course steps and be exempted from the driving test when obtaining a Saudi licence; they must still be 18+, pass the required medical examination and pay the fee (200 SAR). The Saudi licence is issued via Absher / the General Traffic Department using the Iqama.
evidence_quote: hold a valid international or foreign license, please skip to step 5.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: you must retake full driving lessons and tests from scratch. Actually: a valid foreign/international licence exempts you from the test. Action: bring your valid home licence (and an attested translation) to convert it via Absher rather than enrolling in a driving school.

entity_title: Degrees and civil certificates need attestation
fact_text: Educational certificates and marriage contracts must be officially attested to carry legal validity; the Ministry of Foreign Affairs runs the attestation/authentication service (also performed by Saudi missions abroad). Un-attested foreign degrees and civil documents are generally not accepted for professional and family procedures.
evidence_quote: includes the following types: attestation of educational documents - attestation of agencies and marriage contracts

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: your foreign degree and marriage certificate are accepted as-is. Actually: they must be attested/authenticated to have legal validity in the Kingdom. Action: get degrees, and marriage and birth certificates attested (home-country authorities plus the Saudi mission) before relocating, especially for dependent visas and professional roles.

entity_title: Property ownership is restricted for ordinary expats
fact_text: Real-estate ownership rights are limited for foreigners; a Premium Residency Permit holder may own real estate for residential, commercial and industrial purposes, but not in the cities of Mecca and Medina or in border areas. Ordinary sponsored residents typically cannot freely buy residential property.
evidence_quote: Ownership of real estate for residential, commercial, and industrial purposes in areas other than

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed: any expat with money can buy a home in Saudi Arabia. Actually: ownership is restricted and broad rights come with Premium Residency, still excluding Mecca, Medina and border areas. Action: expect to rent unless you hold Premium Residency or a specific ownership approval; do not assume you can purchase a residence on a standard work Iqama.
